### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a335f1defbea57ffe552d2e9efc5ad8d56a2e76a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `52420d612f84575ada576a4aff4200b7a43c7706` — the merge of head `dc70de6236ed9275e90fde37961a7880937c4b0c` into base `a335f1defbea57ffe552d2e9efc5ad8d56a2e76a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 52420d612f84575ada576a4aff4200b7a43c7706 && git checkout 52420d612f84575ada576a4aff4200b7a43c7706
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a335f1defbea57ffe552d2e9efc5ad8d56a2e76a dc70de6236ed9275e90fde37961a7880937c4b0c && git checkout -B drift-repro a335f1defbea57ffe552d2e9efc5ad8d56a2e76a && git merge --no-ff dc70de6236ed9275e90fde37961a7880937c4b0c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a335f1defbea57ffe552d2e9efc5ad8d56a2e76a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dc70de6236ed9275e90fde37961a7880937c4b0c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.approval-escalation-dead-target-refused.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approver-address.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts (`escalateRequest`, `reassignTargetRefusal`), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-node.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-config-refusals.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts and flow-definitions.ts (`registerFlow` → `canonicalizeFlow` → `FlowSchema.parse`), packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts and src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-approval-node-config-contract-refused.ts, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, .changeset/25598-escalation-dead-target-refused.md, packages/spec/src/automation/approval-escalation-dead-target.test.ts, content/docs/references/automation/approval.mdx, docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-node-config.ts. All read at `origin/main` `0a694821` (the merge base) and at the head; none run. Rendered 2026-10-26T14:40Z.

Inputs: card #25598 body and all 9 comments (claim 6415741797, os-dev-report 6417943862, seat answer 6418683750 included), PR #26154 body, file list and net diff against `main` (6 files, +245/−7), and the 48 check-runs on the head: every gate-carrying run `success`, the 7 `skipped` are the opt-in and matrix-placeholder jobs; nothing failed, nothing pending.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of `ApprovalEscalationSchema.escalateTo` narrows** — a trimmed value starting with `team:`, `department:`, `org_membership_level:` or `role:` is refused by a `custom` issue at `escalateTo`, under every `action`. **Right.** `approver-address.ts`: `POSITION_ADDRESS_PREFIXES = ['position:']` and `actingAddresses` yields the user id, the account email and `position:P` only, so no approver acts under any of the four. `escalateRequest` (approval-service.ts ~7168) trims `escalateTo`, reads it under `reassign` (the slate) and under `notify` (audience `[...pending, ...escalatees]`), and leaves it unread under `auto_approve` / `auto_reject` — so the refusal does not depend on `action`, as the hunk says. ADR-0090 D3 makes `role` a reserved-forbidden word, so calling `role:` the retired spelling is accurate.
2. **The accepted shapes are unchanged** — user id, email, bare position machine name, `position:NAME`; only the shape is judged, resolution stays the runtime's (`reassignTargetRefusal`, PR #25600). **Right.** `.superRefine` sits on the inner `z.string()` before `.optional()`, so an omitted target is untouched; §2 of the test pins the four shapes and the omitted case.
3. **The refusal reaches every door the hunks name.** **Right.** `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema.escalation` embeds the schema (approval.zod.ts:1109); `flow-node-config-refusals.ts:174` maps `APPROVAL_NODE_TYPE` to `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema`, so `flowNodeConfigRefusals` reports `node-config-refused-by-contract` at `escalation.escalateTo`; `FlowSchema.parse` carries it to `defineStack` / `defineFlow` / `validate` / `compile` / the save door; `AutomationEngine.registerFlow` (engine.ts:4115) calls `canonicalizeFlow`, which is `FlowSchema.parse` (flow-definitions.ts:209). The executor's own `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema.safeParse` (approval-node.ts:161) refuses consistently. §3 of the test pins the flow path `nodes.1.config.escalation.escalateTo` and the build judge.
4. **No public symbol is added or removed.** **Right.** `DEAD_ESCALATION_TARGET_PREFIXES` and `checkEscalationTargetShape` are module-private; only the `.meta` description changed, and the generated reference page moved with it (`check:generated` inside Build Core, green).
5. **Dropped-refinements ledger grows by `automation/ApprovalEscalation: escalateTo` and `automation/ApprovalNodeConfig: escalation.escalateTo`, totals 245 / 840.** **Right.** A `superRefine` has no projection arm in `refinement-projection.ts`, so the published JSON Schema stays wider than the Zod type; `build-schemas.ts` fails until the ledger matches, and Build Core is green. Consequence to carry: a consumer validating only against `json-schema/**` still accepts a `team:` target and is refused at parse time — the class this ledger exists to record, not a defect of this PR.
6. **D3 entry `approval-escalation-dead-target-refused`.** **Right.** All five `SemanticMigration` fields present; `surface` carries no backticks and no pipes (the sibling `18.flow-approval-node-config-contract-refused` holds the same shape); the id is unique at HEAD; `gen:migration-registry` concatenates `entries/semantic/` by file, so no index edit is owed. No D2 conversion is correct (which position or person a team stood for is the author's judgment); no tombstone is correct (no key removed). The changeset's `adr-0087: registered approval-escalation-dead-target-refused` marker resolves to this entry (Lint gates green).
7. **No in-tree producer writes a dead literal.** **Right.** `git grep` for `escalateTo:` with any of the four prefixes (and `queue:`) returns nothing outside the new test; the Studio inspector field (`flow-node-config.ts:1158`) is an `xRef` position picker, so it cannot emit one. Dogfood Regression Gate green agrees.
8. **Observation, non-blocking:** the prefix match is case-sensitive, so `Team:x` passes the shape check. The card names the lower-case literals, machine names are snake_case, and the runtime predicate still refuses any colon-bearing literal other than `position:` on timeout. Named for the seat under ③; not a defect of this PR.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` **minor** with the BREAKING banner is the correct level: `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (a value an author could write is now refused) takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves, and nothing else in the diff publishes (test, ledger, generated docs). `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right on both the PR body and the changeset body, and the two agree: nothing widens, and the `(narrowing)` arm is owed because `escalateTo` refuses values it used to accept. The changeset carries the Before / Now / Fix migration, both declaration lines and exactly one ADR-0087 marker; Check Changeset and the Lint gates are green. No `skip-changeset`, correctly.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Clause-②` claim line** (dev deviation 1): claim 6415741797 wrote `Clause-②: no` with no arm; the PR body and changeset carry `no (narrowing)`. **Answered:** the PR and changeset lines are the correct ones under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, and the gate "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" is green. **Escalated to the seat** (session_01HbmCEPMBmMLU3VZCEzfec7) to correct the claim's line on the card so the record and the claim agree; not a landing blocker.
- **Serial constraint #25767 / PR #26138** (dev deviation 4, seat answer 6418683750): #26138 is still open at review time (head `a17caaa2`), retires the 16.x-and-older kits only, so this 18.x entry is outside its cut. **Answered as a landing note:** whichever lands first, the other merges `main` and re-checks that `gen:migration-registry` still picks the entry up before the queue, as the seat already said.
- **`open_questions[0]` — refuse `queue:` too?** **Answered** by the seat in 6418683750: option A, keep the card's four, no follow-up card; #25769 (ownership queue, phase 2) carries the question. The diff matches the answer.
- **Dropped-refinements growth** (PR body): the ledger admits two new sites by decision rather than teaching the closed list a prefix-ban arm. **Answered:** accepted — adding a projection arm is a public-contract decision and is not owed on this card; the gap is recorded where consumers read it.
- **`skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md`** (out-of-scope finding 2): its sentence stays true and the path is a governed surface; nothing owed on this PR.
- **Case-sensitive prefix** (① item 8): **escalated to the seat** as an optional tightening (lower-case compare before `startsWith`), the seat's call whether it is worth a card; not required for PASS.
- Deviations 2 (linked worktree) and 3 (model-free trailers) are process notes with no contract bearing.

Seat `domain:spec#4`, session `session_01HbmCEPMBmMLU3VZCEzfec7`, 2026-10-26T14:43Z. Lane review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. The contract face carries its own record, 6418829839 (PASS, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`).

- **Shape.** The PR is a draft against base `main`, and its first line is `Fixes #25598`, which is correct because the PR delivers the whole card. The claim line is corrected on the card by amendment `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` / `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`.

  - The ablation turned 17 refusal pins red and kept 9 acceptance pins green.
